gen-gf-paprika-gf-carlito: Round, open letters keep Carlito easy on the eye even when it shrinks down small. Carlito then tucks in tight beneath Paprika, whose scattered, oversized lowercase does the shouting while the sans quietly holds the line.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-changa: Expressive and loud, Paprika takes the top spot without apology. Changa follows with a lowercase that stands as tall and sturdy as cast iron capitals, so the modern sans-serif never gets drowned out.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-courier-prime: Courier Prime reads like a drafting pen at work, its lowercase filling most of the height with generous round mouths. Paprika's low-contrast arches against that monospace structure make for a lively, mismatched pair.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-days-one: Days One reads big and friendly, its lowercase filling the line. Paprika is best when it makes an entrance with sprawling, expressive letters, while Days One does its best work spacing out text like rungs on a rope ladder.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-epunda-sans: Epunda Sans brings oversized a and e shapes with plenty of daylight inside every curve. Epunda Sans against Paprika makes the sharpest difference: a loud display voice over a quiet, tightly trimmed sans-serif.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-farro: Paprika's lowercase swells up to fill the line like capitals, with a low-contrast stroke that feels bold and unbuttoned. Farro replies with a monoline stroke and compressed ascenders, and that steady sans-serif gives the pair its friendliest edge.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-fragment-mono: Paprika scatters its letters wide and shouts. Fragment Mono lines up beside it like nails on a ruler, with a tall waist line and no shading, so the loose display feels all the freer against that monospace strictness.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-geist-mono: Geist Mono sets fixed-width, code-style letters with a high-rising lowercase and big gaps between them. And Paprika, with its low contrast and no calligraphic shading to guide the eye, gives that monospace grid a loud, expressive neighbor.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-genos: Paprika sprawls its lowercase out to fill the line, with low contrast and a confident swagger. Genos tucks in right after, a plain sans whose glyphs almost touch and whose mild contrast keeps the page moving smoothly.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-geom: Geom lifts a lofty lowercase band over a friendly, contemporary sans, standing tall against Paprika's display swagger. Contrast is the draw.
